summary.text: Antarctic krill is a small swimming crustacean of the Southern Ocean that lives in swarms, sometimes packing 10,000 to 30,000 animals into a cubic metre.
It feeds mainly on phytoplankton, especially very small diatoms, which it strains from the water with a basket formed by its legs.
With a total biomass of about 500 million metric tons, it is one of the most abundant animal species on the planet and a key species in the Antarctic ecosystem.

items.prompt: Krill in an aquarium are given no food for a while. What happens to their bodies after they moult?

options.label: They grow slightly anyway
They come out smaller than before
They stay exactly the same size
They grow faster to find food

items.explain: Unfed krill shrink in size after moulting, which is exceptional for animals of their size.

items.prompt: A researcher wants to tell whether a netted krill has been going hungry. What is a reliable sign?

options.label: Its gut glows a brighter green
Its shell has turned thick and opaque
Its eyes look oversized for its body
Its legs have grown longer bristles

items.explain: A starving krill's body shrinks but its compound eyes do not, so eyes that look too large for the body signal starvation.

items.prompt: Why might shrinking when food runs out be useful to krill in the wild?

options.label: It suits food that runs short each winter
It lets them hide from whales in small cracks
It makes them sink faster to deeper water
It lets them squeeze into denser swarms

items.explain: Shrinking is likely an adaptation to the seasons, since their food is limited in the dark winter months under the ice.

items.prompt: In spring, after a lean winter, where can krill find an extensive energy source besides the open water?

options.label: Dead whales lying on the seabed
Seaweed forests along the coasts
Fish eggs floating at the surface
Algae coating the underside of pack ice

items.explain: Krill scrape the lawn of ice algae from beneath pack ice, a film that can hold more carbon than the water column below, especially valuable in spring.

items.prompt: Krill are messy eaters, spitting out clumps of phytoplankton and leaving strings of waste. What happens to this material?

options.label: It floats and collects at the surface
It sinks very fast into the deep ocean
It dissolves within a few minutes
It gets carried up under the sea ice

items.explain: Both the spat-out clumps and the waste strings, which still hold carbon and diatom shells, are heavy and sink fast into the abyss.

items.prompt: What can Antarctic krill do that no other animal of its size can?

options.label: Hunt fish much larger than itself
Live for decades in cold water
Eat tiny phytoplankton cells directly
Make its own food from sunlight

items.explain: Antarctic krill directly ingest minute phytoplankton cells, which no other animal of krill size can do.
